_comment: Inventory of every third-party CI version this repository pins exactly. Actions may use a release tag (`version`) or an immutable commit (`sha` plus the human-readable `version` comment); tools carry an explicit version variable. `make check-pins` asks the primary upstream whether a newer release exists or, for `github_ref`, whether the monitored major ref moved to a newer commit. A pin without such a monitor rots silently. Floating-major Actions elsewhere remain deliberately absent because they auto-update within their major. Flutter is also absent: .tool-versions plus make check-toolchain is its single source. Semgrep's transitive dependencies remain un-hashed because that would require hundreds of hashes. THIS FILE LIVES UNDER .github/ FOR HISTORY, but governs .forgejo/workflows too; test/pinned_versions_manifest_test.dart keeps workflow and manifest aligned.

actions.purpose: Checks out release source without trusting a mutable major tag.
Restores release caches without trusting a mutable major tag.
Uploads build artifacts through the Forgejo-compatible v3 protocol without trusting its mutable major tag.
Downloads build artifacts through the Forgejo-compatible v3 protocol without trusting its mutable major tag.
Advisory supply-chain scan (Dart-dep CVEs + committed secrets); mirrors `make trivy`.

tools.name: innosetup
tools.purpose: Builds the Windows installer in the mirror's release job (#1208/#1583); the .exe is also sha256-pinned there.
tools._comment: Upstream tags releases `is-7_1_0`, not `7.1.0`, so `tag_regex` names the capture and the underscores are read as dots. Without it every run would report this pin as behind, and an advisory that cries wolf is one nobody reads. The x64 edition is the one downloaded; 7.x keeps backward compatibility with 6.x scripts and the documented breaks are all in Pascal Script and preprocessor functions, which packaging/windows/ocideck.iss deliberately has none of (test/windows_packaging_test.dart forbids a [Code] section outright).

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.purpose: Secret scanning over the working tree and over all history; half of `make check-secrets`.

tools.name: trufflehog
tools.purpose: Secret scanning with per-provider detectors; the other half of `make check-secrets`.

tools.name: semgrep
tools.purpose: SAST over lib/, tool/ and test/ with the local rules in semgrep/ocideck.yaml; `make sast`.
tools.source_note: PyPI and not the GitHub release, because the workflow installs it with pip — 'latest' has to mean the latest version that install path can actually reach.
